authorityTests.note: Each is a cast call with --from set to a specific actor, asserting the exact custom-error selector. Expected selectors are computed with `cast sig`, not hardcoded.

A_agentSurface: guardRepay by deployer (owns every other contract) -> NotAgent
guardRepay by the borrower themselves -> NotAgent
guardRepay by the NAV publisher -> NotAgent
B_borrowerControls: setPolicy by the AGENT -> NotBorrower (the agent cannot widen its own mandate)
revokeAgent by the agent -> NotBorrower (the agent cannot protect itself from revocation)
C_pool: registerRepayer / allowCollateral / accrueQuarterlyCoupon by non-owner -> NotOwner
liquidate a position at 16667 bps -> NotLiquidatable
setPriceFeed a second time -> PriceFeedAlreadySet (write-once holds on-chain)
openPosition when a loan exists -> LoanAlreadyExists
D_factory: deployVault twice for one borrower -> VaultAlreadyExists
deployVault pointing a dUST position at the mXAU feed -> OracleMismatch
deployVault with trigger below MIN -> InvalidTriggerBps
E_oracle: setPrice by the AGENT -> NotPublisher   <- this is the thesis, on-chain
setPrice(0) by the real publisher -> InvalidPrice
getRoundData on a historical round -> OnlyLatestRoundAvailable

stateChangingTests.test: sweepCoupon AGAIN, immediately - the replay bound
stateChangingTests.significance: This is the critical bug found during audit, now proven dead on the deployed contract. Before the fix, couponDue() was a pure function of collateralAmount and never decreased, so this call would have succeeded - 46 more of them would have erased the entire debt with no tokens moving.

stateChangingTests.result: revoked() -> true. guardRepay() and sweepCoupon() from the agent now both revert Refused_AgentRevoked (0x0951234f). There is no un-revoke.
stateChangingTests.significance: The borrower's kill switch works on-chain. The rehearsal vault is now permanently disarmed, which is why this test ran last.

destructiveTests.note: Initially skipped as too risky, then run in full on a THIRD, sacrificial position. The trick was collateral choice: the victim position was collateralised in mXAU, which has its own NavOracle (0x16c683d9...). Dropping the mXAU NAV never touches the dUST feed, so the demo position stayed at 16667 bps the entire time and was never exposed to a passing liquidator.

liquidate.setup: publisher address opened a 10000e18 mXAU / 6000e6 dUSD position (16667 bps), deployer funded itself with dUSD and approved the pool as liquidator

step1_graceDelays.reading: an open grace window delays liquidation of an already-unhealthy position

step2_priceDrop.reading: below LIQUIDATION_BPS 11000, and the demo position is untouched because it prices off a different feed

step3_liquidation.sum: 10000000000000000000000 - exactly the pledged collateral, to the wei

liquidate.arithmeticCheck: owedUnits = 6000 / 0.65 = 9230.769230..., seized = owedUnits * 1.05 = 9692.307692..., refund = 10000 - seized = 307.692307.... Matches the on-chain numbers exactly.
liquidate.significance: The predecessor system's seizure step was `pure ()` and never moved a token. This one moves 9692 units of collateral to the liquidator and refunds the remainder to the borrower, in one transaction, callable by anyone.

withdrawCollateral_success.setup: on the rehearsal position: registerRepayer(deployer), then applyRepayment(deployer, 5128879310) to clear the debt
withdrawCollateral_success.result: debt 5128879310 -> 0, then 10000e18 dUST released back to the borrower, collateralOf -> 0
withdrawCollateral_success.reading: collateral is escrowed, not confiscated - once the debt is gone the borrower takes it back

transferPublisher_success.target: the mXAU oracle only - the dUST feed the demo depends on was never touched
transferPublisher_success.incidentNote: The restore transaction first failed with 'nonce too low' (a race between two sends from the same key), leaving the deployer holding the mXAU publisher role for a few blocks. Caught on the next read and restored. No demo dependency was affected, since the demo prices off dUST.

allowCollateral_and_setPriceFeed_firstWr.result: collateralInfo -> (true, false, 18, 'tTST', 0x16c683d9...), and a SECOND setPriceFeed on the same token reverts PriceFeedAlreadySet (0x5e3b8265)
allowCollateral_and_setPriceFeed_firstWr.reading: write-once is enforced per token, not globally - a new instrument can still be registered, but an existing one can never be repointed

coverageSummary.everyFunctionOnEveryDeployedContract: exercised - reads, authority refusals, and success paths
coverageSummary.residue: 0x...bEEF is registered as a collateral instrument named tTST pointing at the mXAU feed. It is inert - no position can be opened against it because the token address holds no ERC20 code. Harmless, but it is in the pool's registry and should be mentioned rather than hidden.
